newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - Oct 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - Oct 9.

text.p: These are significant stories in the Ivorian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ivory Coast and its commercial bank creditors fail to reach common ground on rescheduling $6 billion of trade debt, finance minister N'Goran Niamen says. Talks to resume in November.

- Ivory Coast phone monopoly CI-TELCOM needs 600 billion CFA francs in investment to expand telephone network to meet demand by 100,000 waiting subscribers, director general Brou N'Gbla says in interview. The government is examining bids from international companies for takeover of CI-TELCOM which is to be privatised later this year.

- President Henri Konan Bedie to visit opposition stronghold of Gangoa, central Ivory Coast, on November 15, which is National Peace Day. Gangoa was rocked by poll violence during presidential elections a year ago won by Bedie.
- Environment ministry to organise roundtable on October 15-16 to raise funds for it's action plan for the environment.

- Partial elections likely to be staged on December 29 in opposition strongholds, notably around central Gangoa, where voting in legislative and local elections was put off because of violence around the presidential ballot last October.
